title: Does a diagonal cut a rectangle's corner into equal angles?
description: A rectangle six centimetres by four is drawn with the diagonal PR, and the two angles at each end are measured with a protractor. Keeko's doubt is that the diagonal cuts each corner into two equal angles.
teaching_notes: One idea: a diagonal splits a right-angled corner of a rectangle into two angles that add up to a right angle, and they are equal only in a square. Watch for students who think a diagonal always bisects the corner.

source: In rectangle PQRS the diagonal PR divides angle R into g and
video_script.why: A learner predicts and measures the angles a diagonal makes with the sides of a rectangle, and finds that each pair adds up to a right angle.
video_script.substitution: the book's own rectangle PQRS with the diagonal PR, drawn six centimetres by four centimetres
video_script.anchor: a rectangle PQRS with the diagonal PR cutting the corners at P and R into smaller angles
video_script.wrong_answer: the diagonal cuts each corner into two equal angles
video_script.wrong_move: assumes a diagonal always splits a corner exactly in half, without measuring
video_script.payoff_line: The two angles are not equal, but they add up to ninety degrees.

final_answer.value: g and h are not equal unless the rectangle is a square; c and d are not equal unless the rectangle is a square. In every rectangle g + h = 90 degrees and c + d = 90 degrees

maths_rules: each corner of a rectangle is a right angle, 90 degrees
for a 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle, the diagonal makes angles of about 34 degrees and 56 degrees with the sides
34 degrees + 56 degrees = 90 degrees, so the pair fills the corner
in a square both angles are 45 degrees, so the angles are equal only in a square
video_script.design: The rectangle and its diagonal are drawn, the angles are measured at both ends, and each pair is added to compare with the corner.
